manual.repo: That's {{path}} in the Muster repo, which the app doesn't open: read it on GitHub or in your editor.
manual.web: Web links don't open from the manual: {{url}}
manual.noCommandsPage: the core sent no Commands page

new-task.what: Open New task in the pane beside the board

close-pane.what: Close the pane: a task, a note or New task
close-pane.where: Anywhere while the pane is open, except in the search box or a view's name, which take Esc for themselves

search.what: Put the caret in the search box, with its words selected so typing replaces them. Ctrl+F is left to text fields, where it moves the caret
search.where: Anywhere in the window. From a tab without a search box, it opens the board first

focus-mode.what: Turn Focus on, or back off to the mode you were in (the display modes are in Settings, Display)

zoom-in.what: Make everything larger: the board, the panes and the manual (the size is remembered; also in Settings, Appearance, Text size)

resize-pane.what: Move the edge of the pane or the projects sidebar 40 pixels: → to the right, ← to the left, in either reading direction (the width is remembered)
resize-pane.where: The edge of the pane or the projects sidebar, once Tab has put the focus on it

resize-pane-big.what: The same in steps of 120 pixels
resize-pane-big.where: The edge of the pane or the projects sidebar, once Tab has put the focus on it

send.what: Create the task, send the answer or the comment, file the note, send to the helper, or send a task back
send.where: New task's description, an answer box, the comment box, a note's File as task form, the Helper, and the task pane's Send back form

discard-text.what: Leave the editor or empty the comment box. With typed text, the first Esc only warns and the second throws the text away
discard-text.where: A task's write-up after Edit, and the comment box

rename-cancel.what: Stop renaming and keep the old title (↩ saves the new one)
rename-cancel.where: A task's title, after clicking it

choice-close.what: Fold the choices back without changing the value
choice-close.where: Priority and Type, while their choices are laid out

estimate-save.what: Save the estimate (leaving the field saves it too)
estimate-save.where: The Est fields: agent time, test time, tokens

tag-add.where: The tag field, in a task or in New task

release-cancel.what: Don't release it: nothing changes, and the focus goes back to Release
release-cancel.where: Release's confirm, in the task pane's Next step, on a claim no session can be reached on

search-clear.what: Clear the search, or leave the box when it's already empty. It never closes the pane
search-clear.where: The search box above Board, Table, Timeline and Graph

view-save.what: Save the search, filters and sort as a view under the name you typed
view-save.where: A view's name, after + Save view

view-cancel.what: Stop naming the view; nothing is saved
view-cancel.where: A view's name, after + Save view

quick-add.what: Add the line to the backlog as a note
quick-add.where: Add to the backlog…, at the top of the Backlog column, or of the Backlog band under Group by

quick-add-clear.where: Add to the backlog…, at the top of the Backlog column, or of the Backlog band under Group by

accept-all-cancel.where: Accept all's confirm, in Your check's Just accept group (the board and Waiting for you)

grid-move.what: Move to the next cell of the Feature grid: across the stages, or down the features (← and → swap right to left, where the arrows follow the reading direction); ← from Backlog goes to the feature's name, which ↩ opens. Inside a cell, ↑ and ↓ step through its cards and +N more
grid-move.where: The Feature grid, once Tab has put the focus on it (the grid is one stop for Tab)

grid-ends.what: Go to the row's first cell (Backlog) or its last (Done today)
grid-ends.where: A cell of the Feature grid, once Tab has put the focus on it

grid-enter.what: Go into the cell, to its first card (or its +N more); ↩ on a card opens it in the pane beside the board
grid-enter.where: A cell of the Feature grid, once Tab has put the focus on it

grid-leave.what: Back from a card to its cell; the pane stays open
grid-leave.where: A card or +N more in the Feature grid

label-save.what: Save the label or the category (leaving the field saves it too; in Settings it's saved as you type)
label-save.where: A project's label or category in Settings, Projects; in the sidebar, a project's name after a double click, a heading's name after a double click or ↩, and + Category's field

label-revert.what: Keep the label or the category as it was before you started typing
label-revert.where: A project's label or category in Settings, Projects; in the sidebar, a project's name after a double click, a heading's name after a double click or ↩, and + Category's field

move-up.what: Move the project or the heading up one place, its projects with it. A project at the top of its heading goes to the end of the one above. The first move picks the Mine order
move-up.where: A project or a category heading in the sidebar, once Tab has put the focus on it

move-down.what: Move the project or the heading down one place. A project at the bottom of its heading goes to the top of the one below
move-down.where: A project or a category heading in the sidebar, once Tab has put the focus on it

heading-rename.what: Rename the heading in place (a double click does too). A name another heading has puts the two together
heading-rename.where: A category heading in the sidebar, once Tab has put the focus on it

heading-fold.what: Fold the heading to its name and counts (its chevron does too); the selected project and the ones that need you still show on it (→ right to left, where the arrows follow the reading direction)
heading-fold.where: A category heading in the sidebar, once Tab has put the focus on it

heading-unfold.what: Unfold the heading (← right to left)
heading-unfold.where: A category heading in the sidebar, once Tab has put the focus on it

colour-close.what: Fold the colours back without changing the project's colour
colour-close.where: A project's colours in the sidebar, after a click on its dot

page.intro: Every keyboard shortcut in the app, and the slash commands for Claude Code. This page is made from the app's own table of shortcuts, and a test checks every key the app reacts to against that table, so a shortcut can't exist without being listed here. ⌘ is the Command key. {{ctrl}}{{option}} ↩ is Return.
page.ctrl: Ctrl works too wherever ⌘ is shown.
page.ctrlExceptOne: Ctrl works too wherever ⌘ is shown, except {{list}}, which takes ⌘ only.
page.ctrlExceptMany: Ctrl works too wherever ⌘ is shown, except {{list}}, which take ⌘ only.
page.slashIntro: `/mu` (or the long form, `/muster`) runs one `muster` command from inside a Claude Code session. The first word picks what it does, and anything that isn't a route is captured as a backlog one-liner, never guessed. Routes for the owner answer in plain words; routes for agents and the system print what `muster` printed.
page.slashRouter: The router is built (task 0003) but not installed yet: it goes into the personal layer once the owner says yes. Until then, type `! muster …` in a session, as [For agents](07-for-agents.md#in-a-claude-code-session) shows.

what.status: What's waiting for you, then the queue in one line
what.add: Put a one-liner in the backlog
what.answer: Answer a question; it reaches the agent that asked
what.capture: Captured as a backlog one-liner, never run as a command
what.ask: Ask without stopping; the answer is pushed back
what.next: Claim the top Ready task you may take
what.note: A line in the task's log
what.pass: Hand the task on to the next stage
what.return: Send it back a stage, with the reason
what.block: Mark it blocked, and why: tasks, you, a permission, a question or outside
what.help: The routes, then muster's own help
